outcome: Migrate the Rust runtime (crates/graphrefly) to the D797 kernel rule set (activated by graphrefly:D798, revised by graphrefly:D799) as a self-contained Rust package under graphrefly:D800, changing only the contract deltas the B140 runtime-owner handoff lists and keeping what works today, and qualify each kernel scenario with source-bound Rust evidence
acceptance: Scope: the existing crate is changed to the rules active by graphrefly:D798/D799, following graphrefly sessions/active/HANDOFF-B140-runtime-owners.md. Everything is pre-0.1 (the user, 2026-11-10): no shim, deprecated alias, old name or compatibility option is kept, and no API keeps an old shape only for continuity; existing code that is already the simplest clean form stays, and code shaped only by history is replaced by the simplest form the rules allow. Root reference/kernel and reference/modules are read for behavior only; no code is copied from them, and their tests are not Rust evidence. The implementation follows this crate's architecture and Rust idiom (single-thread Rc/RefCell, no unsafe, no async in the core).

Phase 1, messages: Message has exactly seven variants, START, PENDING, DATA, RESOLVED, INVALIDATE, COMPLETE, ERROR. Dirty is renamed Pending; Teardown, Pause, Resume and Pull are removed, with LockId, PullDemand, Tier, is_up_allowed, Pausable and the pause lockset and buffer; the upward channel is removed (Node::up, Node::up_toward, Ctx::up, up_toward, up_next, up_next_toward, DeferredCtx::up, Core::up and its routing). ctx.down rejects START, PENDING and RESOLVED (START since graphrefly:D801, R-subscription@3 and R-failure@3); uncaught, the rejection is the node's ERROR. In Rust the four retired types are unrepresentable in process, and the public Tier type and observe events' tier go. The crate's canonical protobuf codec (adapters/bridge_protobuf.rs, hand-written, no generated code) carries no Message or Wave, so it has no message numbers to change. Its WireEdgeKind DIRTY is renamed PENDING in names only (CanonicalWireEdgeKind::Pending, WIRE_EDGE_KIND_PENDING = 1, the issue codes wire-edge-group-duplicate-pending and wire-edge-group-data-before-pending, the status counter pending), with bytes and bridge behavior unchanged (the user's choice of 2026-11-10). The retired surfaces' production uses move in the same phase, as the graphrefly-rs decision on retired surfaces records: the pull_id holders (data_structures 5, messaging 4, work_queue 3) and the work_queue admission pager's up_next PULL; the TEARDOWN reactors and SyncValueFromError::Teardown; Pausable on the sources; worker.rs's [RESOLVED] becomes sending nothing; HostBoundaryAbort and host_boundary.rs go with their dispatcher, boundary, subscribe and batch handlers. crates/graphrefly-bindings-py is taken out of the workspace build (workspace exclude) without being fixed or deleted. Passes C-26, C-42 and C-12 (c).

Phase 2, waves: the kernel puts a PENDING prefix on every array carrying DATA, RESOLVED, INVALIDATE, COMPLETE or ERROR and marks the sender's dependents pending; a pending node that sent nothing gets exactly one kernel RESOLVED; a quiet node marks nothing pending. Each ctx.down call is one array, in written order with no tier sort (Core::down's sort and the batch's last-slice-per-node overwrite go), a terminal last, split at its last INVALIDATE, delivered after the function returns. The snapshot for a subscriber or new dependent is the DATA values of the last array that carried DATA, then the terminal; subscribe no longer sends DIRTY. A batch's writes to one node commit as one accumulated array. Host input is a state handle only (graphrefly-rs:D3): Graph::state, Node::state and their empty forms return State<T>, whose set, invalidate, complete and error are the only host inputs (set's function form lands in phase 5); the public Node::down, GraphNode::down and Node::set go, so raw arrays leave only through ctx.down and DeferredCtx::down; a subscriber's sink is Fn(&[Message<AnyValue>]), called once per array, START array included. Passes C-12, C-16, C-23 and C-41, the array, prefix and rejection clauses of C-28, and the value and quiet-node clauses of C-44.

Phase 3, terminals and invalidation: COMPLETE, ERROR and INVALIDATE each take an auto or manual policy per node, default auto. Under auto ERROR an INVALIDATE earlier in the wave applies first. Under manual INVALIDATE ctx.deps[i] says whether an INVALIDATE arrived. A node that ends closes its lifetime at once and releases its dependencies; an ended node can still be subscribed, depended on and added, its snapshot carrying its terminal (subscribing to or adding a terminal node no longer panics); host input to it is refused. Passes C-3, C-15, C-17 and C-36, C-40 except its replace clause, the terminal and manual-INVALIDATE clauses of C-44, and the terminal clauses of C-34.

Phase 4, lifetime: an optional setup, owned by the instance, runs once per lifetime just before the first run with that run's ctx and may return the lifetime's cleanup. It replaces Ctx::on_deactivation and Ctx::on_invalidate at every call site (the 17 production on_deactivation callers in sources, graph effect, adapters/environment, adapters/bridge and worker; Graph::effect keeps its latest per-run cleanup in private state). ctx gains the lifetime's abort signal. Closing aborts the signal, releases dependencies, runs the cleanup (which may still read private state) and then drops private state, also when the node ends. Output and requests through a closed lifetime's ctx are dropped; status is derived. Passes C-4, and the lifetime clauses of C-33 and C-34.

Phase 5, requests: host inputs, subscribe, unsubscribe, replace, rewire and batch commits made during a wave queue and run in order after it; a function's write to its own upstream is such a request, so the synchronous-feedback-cycle panic and the inline nested-mutator path go. batch(body) runs body at once and returns its result; its commit is one wave and is itself a queued request, with its topology requests after the commit; a throwing body commits nothing. State<T>::set takes a value or StateWrite::from_fn(f), with f: FnOnce(Option<&T>) -> Option<T> (graphrefly-rs:D3); the function computes from the value when the write runs, and returning None writes nothing, the Rust form of a function returning the value it was given. replace(id, deps, fn, { setup, recipe }) gives a new instance under the same id and subscribers; definition(id) reads it. ctx.rewire(deps), scoped to the lifetime and undone when it closes, replaces the rewire_next_* calls (higher_order, time); the host-level Node::replace_deps, subscribe_dep and unsubscribe_dep go, and each production caller (process, messaging, adapters/bridge, data_structures) is moved to replace, to ctx.rewire or to a state input, as the owner decides per call site after a read-only check at the start of the phase (graphrefly-rs:D4), each decision recorded. Cycle checks look through current and declared dependencies. Passes C-6, C-11, C-29, C-33, C-34, C-35, C-37, the replace clause of C-40 and the rest of C-28.

Phase 6, cross-graph (graphrefly:D803 and D804, R-bridge@2, R-graph-domain@3; the hold is lifted): each graph's arena owns its wave scope, request queue and batch frame, so graphs on one thread share none of them (C-47); wire edge groups take the reference module's shape (one WireEdgeCause frame per sender wave, a gate that releases a session's causes in order and at most once, inbound nodes over the gate, an issues node); the per-edge PENDING/DATA frames, cohorts, tombstones, release drain and status node and the bridge's FanInSources go with no shim; the codec moves to WireEdgeCause and the new fixtures. Passes C-1, C-1b and C-47, and requalifies C-1a; C-1c is unchanged.

Checkpoint stage, after phase 5 (graphrefly:D802, graphrefly-rs:D5): crates/graphrefly's checkpoint follows R-checkpoint@1, the eight items of the root handoff's 'Checkpoint after D802' section: capture only at a wave boundary; a restored graph has no subscribers and restored nodes get no waves before their first activation; per-dependency received inputs saved, and the first activation runs once on changed dependencies only; setup runs at the restored first activation; recipe and setup per instance, a replace without a recipe making the node local-only; nodes built after their declared dependencies, ctx.rewire lifetime dependencies saved; an ended node restored ended without private state, its ERROR payload saved as JSON; no D109 version field or restore checks, and a checkpoint lacking what the rule saves refused. Passes C-38; C-45 and C-46 wait for their modules.

Rust sugar: the first-run gate (NodeOpts.partial and all_deps_settled) and the opt-in equality operators (distinct_until_changed, settle_by) stay, and the rustdoc says they are Rust sugar, not protocol; the crate has no dynamic reads.

Each phase ends with the crate's checks passing (cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy -p graphrefly-rs --all-targets, cargo test -p graphrefly-rs, cargo doc, the stale-phrase scan, run through scripts/run-logged.sh) and that phase's scenarios passing; it is then committed and pushed to d797-kernel-migration only (graphrefly-rs:D4). Existing tests that check a replaced or retired rule are rewritten for the current rule or removed, and each removal is listed in the phase report.

Evidence: each scenario is reported with runtime rust, the test command, the result and the source commit, recorded on this item. Root spec/conformance.jsonl runtimes flags are not changed here (graphrefly:D784); the root records the evidence. Scenarios that also check a draft module rule (C-2, C-5, C-9, C-10, C-13, C-27, C-30, C-31, C-32, C-39, C-43, C-45, C-46) are out of scope; C-38 is in the checkpoint stage.
